summary: macOS SSO client cert chain rotation breaks device-trust evaluation and blocks console/CLI logins
description:
Issue summary:
On 2026-03-08 at ~09:12 UTC we observed a spike in authentication failures for macOS users using the native Redwood SSO client (idp-agent). Affected users could not obtain a console session or authenticate the CLI; web SAML flows (browser) largely worked. Error signals pointed to device-trust evaluation failing due to an untrusted client certificate chain after the IdP certificate rotation.

Impact:
- ~120 unique macOS users reported being unable to open the Electron Console or authenticate the CLI between 09:10 and 11:45 UTC.
- CI jobs triggered by service accounts on macOS build runners failed to authenticate, causing some pipelines to abort (partial impact).
- No customer-facing hosted API impact observed.

Environment:
- Production (us-west) Okta IdP instance and our idp-agent (macOS) versions 1.3.2 and 1.3.3.
- Device-trust verification service (internal) v2.1.

Steps to reproduce (internal test):
1. Install idp-agent macOS 1.3.2 on a test host.
2. Trigger an interactive SSO flow (open Console) and observe device-trust token exchange.
3. Rotate IdP intermediate cert chain on test IdP (mirror of production rotation).
4. Attempt SSO; device-trust returns 401 and login fails.

Observed logs and errors:
- idp-agent (macOS): "TLS handshake failed: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority"
- device-trust service: "device attestation: client cert verification failed: x509: certificate is not authorized for any purpose"
- Console/Electron: 403 with message "device-trust validation failed"
- SRE dashboard (auth-errors) spike: +450% 401/403 auth rejects for macOS user-agent across 09:08-10:00 UTC

Investigation notes:
- Timeline correlates with automated IdP certificate rotation event at 09:05 UTC. Rotation process replaced the intermediate CA bundle published to the IdP but the code-signed macOS idp-agent binaries still contain the previous CA bundle.
- The macOS SSO client anchors validation to the bundled CA for offline device attestation (design decision to avoid OS CA changes). The agent failed to trust the new intermediate chain, so it did not present a verifiable client cert to the IdP.
- Linux and Windows SSO agents pull the CA bundle at runtime from the identity-config service and were updated successfully during rotation; macOS clients require a client-side agent update. Hence browser SAML (which relies on browser trust store) continued to work.
- Early hypothesis: missing agent binary rollout for macOS + stale bundled CA. Confirmed by reproducer in staging and by examining idp-agent 1.3.2 binary contents.

Immediate workaround applied:
- Temporary rollback of the IdP intermediate chain to the previous bundle at 10:15 UTC restored macOS login for ~90% of affected users.
- For users still failing, Support provided a manual web SAML login path and advised to use a Linux VM for CLI-critical workflows.

Fix deployed / next steps:
- A patch PR was merged to idp-agent to add a runtime CA refresh fallback for macOS and updated to bundle the rotated intermediate (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-agent/pull/402).
- Release idp-agent 1.3.4 with CA refresh logic and push via MDM. Canary MDM deployment started 2026-03-09 20:00 UTC.
- Full fleet rollout scheduled 2026-03-11 04:00 UTC (after additional testing and coordination with Desktop Ops).
- Add explicit pre-rotation verification step to the SSO rotation runbook to verify agent compatibility and automated MDM rollout for macOS agents.

Post-incident actions (PIR items):
- Update SSO cert rotation playbook to include macOS agent compatibility check and MDM rollout window.
- Create monitoring alert for agent CA chain mismatch (signature-based) to detect before rotation.
- Document a permanent client behavior: macOS idp-agent must support dynamic CA fetch or be scheduled for MDM updates before IdP chain rotations.

Status and recovery:
- Root cause identified: macOS idp-agent bundled CA out-of-sync with IdP rotation.
- Immediate rollback restored most users; full remediation requires agent rollout which is in progress.
comments: Support (Jordan Liu) 2026-03-08 09:25 UTC: Multiple macOS users reporting 403 device-trust failures. Opening ticket and tagging Identity and SRE. See Slack thread: #idp - https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C0123456789/p1678264321000123

Identity (Diego Morales) 2026-03-08 09:48 UTC: Confirmed IdP rotation occurred at 09:05 UTC. Reproduced locally with staging rotation — macOS agent failed because of bundled CA. Hypothesis: agent binary wasn't included in the rotation rollout. Assigning to Desktop Ops for MDM push plan.

SRE (Priya Nair) 2026-03-08 10:08 UTC: Rolled back intermediate chain at IdP to previous bundle at 10:15 UTC. Auth errors dropped back to baseline by 10:40 UTC. Continuing to monitor. Creating alert rule for CA mismatch anomaly.
Reporter (Aisha Patel) 2026-03-09 15:02 UTC: Thanks — macOS users on my team regained access after the rollback. Will coordinate with Desktop Ops for the agent update window.

Desktop Ops (Lena Korhonen) 2026-03-10 11:30 UTC: Canary MDM push for idp-agent 1.3.4 started. No regressions so far in canaries. Full fleet rollout scheduled 2026-03-11 04:00 UTC with a 30-minute maintenance window notice to staff.
